records.source: וַיַּ֣רְא הָעָ֔ם כִּֽי־בֹשֵׁ֥שׁ מֹשֶׁ֖ה לָרֶ֣דֶת מִן־הָהָ֑ר וַיִּקָּהֵ֨ל הָעָ֜ם עַֽל־אַהֲרֹ֗ן וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ אֵלָיו֙ ק֣וּם׀עֲשֵׂה־לָ֣נוּ אֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֵֽלְכוּ֙ לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ כִּי־זֶ֣ה׀מֹשֶׁ֣ה הָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶֽעֱלָ֨נוּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְנוּ מֶה־הָ֥יָה לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And saw the people that delayed Moses to come down from the mountain, and assembled the people against Aaron and said to him, arise, make for us gods who will go before us, for this Moses, the man who brought us up from [the] land of Egypt, not we know what has happened to him.
pieces: The people saw that Moses was a long time in coming down from the mountain. So they crowded around Aaron and said to him, "Get up and make us gods to lead the way for us. This Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt, we have no idea what has become of him."

L.1: And the people saw that Moses delayed to come down from the mountain, and the people gathered around Aaron and said to him, "Arise, make for us gods who will go before us, for this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him."

R.1: Moses stayed on the mountain a long time. When the people saw that he was not coming down, they crowded around Aaron. They said, "Come on, make us gods to lead us. We do not know what has happened to Moses, the man who led us out of Egypt."

decisions.choice: gods: plural, since the verb with it is plural
alternatives: make us a god who will go before us
decisions.reason: The word can mean the one God or many gods. When it means Israel's God it takes singular verbs; here the verb "will go" is plural, so the people ask for gods. Yet Aaron makes a single calf and proclaims a feast to Yahweh (verses 4-5), so they may have meant an image standing for Israel's own God. Nehemiah 9:18 retells the story with the singular, "This is your god"; Acts 7:40 quotes the request as "Make us gods".

decisions.choice: delayed: was long in coming
decisions.reason: Moses had gone up into the cloud on the mountain and stayed there forty days and forty nights (24:18). To the people below, he seemed lost.

decisions.choice: this Moses, the man: spoken with scorn
decisions.reason: "This Moses" sets him at a distance. The people credit Moses, not God, with bringing them out of Egypt, and now they want something else to go before them, in place of the God who went before them in the pillar of cloud (13:21).

decisions.choice: Get up / Come on ... to lead the way
decisions.reason: "Arise" urges Aaron to act at once; Balanced and Readable use everyday words for it. "Go before us" means to lead, as the pillar of cloud did; Literal keeps "go before".

records.heading: The calf of gold

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ אַהֲרֹ֔ן פָּֽרְקוּ֙ נִזְמֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאָזְנֵ֣י נְשֵׁיכֶ֔ם בְּנֵיכֶ֖ם וּבְנֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וְהָבִ֖יאוּ אֵלָֽי׃
records.gloss: And said to them Aaron, tear off [the] rings of the gold which [are] in [the] ears of your wives, your sons and your daughters, and bring [them] to me.
pieces: Aaron told them, "Pull the gold rings out of the ears of your wives and your sons and daughters, and bring them here to me."

L.2: And Aaron said to them, "Tear off the rings of gold that [are] in the ears of your wives, your sons and your daughters, and bring [them] to me."

R.2: Aaron answered, "Get the gold earrings from your wives, your sons and your daughters. Bring them to me."

decisions.choice: the rings of gold: likely jewelry asked from the Egyptians
decisions.reason: Israel left Egypt with articles of silver and gold given by the Egyptians (3:22; 11:2; 12:35-36). The gold God gave his people on the way out is now gathered for an idol. Later the people give their jewelry freely for the tabernacle (35:22).

decisions.choice: tear off: remove with force
decisions.reason: The verb means to tear away or strip off. The same verb is used in verse 3 and verse 24.

records.source: וַיִּתְפָּֽרְקוּ֙ כָּל־הָעָ֔ם אֶת־נִזְמֵ֥י הַזָּהָ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּאָזְנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיָּבִ֖יאוּ אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹֽן׃
records.gloss: And tore off from themselves all the people the rings of the gold which [were] in their ears, and they brought [them] to Aaron.
pieces: So all the people stripped the gold rings from their ears and brought them to Aaron.

L.3: And all the people tore off the rings of gold that [were] in their ears and brought [them] to Aaron.

R.3: Everyone pulled off their gold earrings and handed them over to Aaron.

decisions.choice: all the people tore off from themselves: every one of them took part, at once
decisions.reason: The verb form means they stripped the rings off themselves. "All the people" stresses that the whole people joined in, as readily as they had once said, "All that Yahweh has spoken we will do" (24:3).

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֣ח מִיָּדָ֗ם וַיָּ֤צַר אֹתוֹ֙ בַּחֶ֔רֶט וַֽיַּעֲשֵׂ֖הוּ עֵ֣גֶל מַסֵּכָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵ֤לֶּה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱל֖וּךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And he took [it] from their hand and he fashioned it with the tool and he made it a calf of cast metal. And they said, these [are] your gods, Israel, who brought you up from [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: He took the gold from them, shaped it with an engraving tool, and made it into a calf of cast metal. Then they said, "Israel, these are your gods, who brought you up from the land of Egypt!"

L.4: And he took [it] from their hand and fashioned it with an engraving tool and made it a calf of cast metal. And they said, "These [are] your gods, O Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt."

R.4: Aaron took the gold from them and shaped it with a tool. He made it into a statue of a young bull out of melted metal. Then the people said, "Israel, here are your gods who brought you out of Egypt!"

decisions.choice: fashioned it with an engraving tool: the exact process is uncertain
alternatives: tied it up in a bag
decisions.reason: The word for the tool is used elsewhere only of a stylus for writing (Isaiah 8:1). It may mean Aaron shaped or finished the gold with a carving tool. Some take the verb and noun differently: that he formed it in a mold, or that he tied the gold up in a bag (a similar word means "bags" in 2 Kings 5:23). The result is clear either way: a calf of cast metal.

decisions.choice: a calf of cast metal: an image of a young bull
decisions.reason: The word means a young bull, a picture of strength. Images of bulls were used in the religions of Egypt and Canaan, and a god could be shown standing on one. The metal was melted and poured, so this is a cast image, which God's law had just forbidden (20:4, 23; 34:17).

decisions.choice: these are your gods: plural, though there is one calf
alternatives: This is your god, O Israel, who brought you up
decisions.reason: Both the word and the verb "brought you up" are plural, as in verse 1. Jeroboam later says the same words over his two golden calves (1 Kings 12:28). Nehemiah 9:18 retells this verse with the singular, "This is your god who brought you up from Egypt".

decisions.choice: a statue of a young bull out of melted metal
decisions.reason: Readable says what a "calf of cast metal" is: an image of a young bull, made from melted metal. It says "calf" from then on.

records.source: וַיַּ֣רְא אַהֲרֹ֔ן וַיִּ֥בֶן מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לְפָנָ֑יו וַיִּקְרָ֤א אַֽהֲרֹן֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר חַ֥ג לַיהוָ֖ה מָחָֽר׃
records.gloss: And saw Aaron and he built an altar before it, and called Aaron and said, a feast to Yahweh [is] tomorrow.
pieces: When Aaron saw this, he built an altar in front of the calf and made a proclamation: "Tomorrow we hold a feast to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.5: And Aaron saw [it], and he built an altar before it. And Aaron called out and said, "A feast to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} tomorrow!"

R.5: When Aaron saw this, he built an altar in front of the calf. Then he announced, "Tomorrow we will have a feast to honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!"

decisions.choice: Aaron saw: what he saw is not stated
alternatives: Aaron was afraid (the same consonants can be read as "he feared")
decisions.reason: He saw the calf, or saw how the people received it (verse 4). Either way, his next steps lend the calf the forms of true worship.

decisions.choice: a feast to Yahweh: the calf is honored under the name of Israel's God
decisions.reason: Aaron does not proclaim a feast to a foreign god but to Yahweh. The sin is not only turning to other gods but making an image to stand for the true God, which the second of the Ten Words forbids (20:4-5).

decisions.choice: in front of the calf
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "before it"; Balanced and Readable name the calf.

records.source: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֨ימוּ֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיַּעֲל֣וּ עֹלֹ֔ת וַיַּגִּ֖שׁוּ שְׁלָמִ֑ים וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב הָעָם֙ לֶֽאֱכֹ֣ל וְשָׁת֔וֹ וַיָּקֻ֖מוּ לְצַחֵֽק׃פ
records.gloss: And they rose early on [the] next day and offered up burnt offerings and brought near peace offerings. And sat the people to eat and to drink, and they rose up to play.
pieces: They were up early the next morning, offering burnt offerings and bringing fellowship offerings. Then the people sat down to a meal of food and drink, and rose up to revel.

L.6: And they rose early on the next day and offered up burnt offerings and brought near peace offerings. And the people sat down to eat and to drink, and they rose up to play.

R.6: The next morning the people got up early. They offered burnt offerings and brought fellowship offerings. They sat down to eat and drink. Then they got up and began to party wildly.

decisions.choice: to play: to revel, with loud and unrestrained celebration
decisions.reason: The verb means to laugh, play or make sport. It is used of Isaac caressing Rebekah (Genesis 26:8) and of mocking (Genesis 39:14, 17). Here it goes with the dancing of verse 19 and the people "broken loose" of verse 25: wild feasting before the idol, which may have included sexual play. Paul quotes this verse in 1 Corinthians 10:7 as a warning against idolatry, and warns against sexual immorality in the next verse.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings, peace offerings, eating and drinking: a twisted copy of the covenant meal
decisions.reason: When the covenant was made, Israel offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and the elders ate and drank in God's presence (24:5, 11). Now the same acts are done before the calf.

decisions.choice: revel / party wildly
decisions.reason: "Play" sounds like children's games in English. Balanced says "revel" and Readable "party wildly" for the noisy celebration meant (m1). Literal keeps "play". Balanced and Readable say "fellowship offerings", Literal "peace offerings".

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה לֶךְ־רֵ֕ד כִּ֚י שִׁחֵ֣ת עַמְּךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱלֵ֖יתָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, go, go down, for has acted corruptly your people whom you brought up from [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Go down at once! Your people, whom you brought up from the land of Egypt, have acted corruptly.

L.7: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, "Go, go down, for your people whom you brought up from the land of Egypt have acted corruptly.

R.7: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told Moses, "Hurry back down! Your people, the ones you led out of Egypt, have done something terrible.

decisions.choice: your people, whom you brought up: God speaks of them as Moses' people
decisions.reason: God has called Israel "my people" (3:7, 10; 5:1). Here he calls them Moses' people, whom Moses brought up, the very words the people used of Moses in verse 1. In verse 11 Moses answers that they are God's people, whom God brought out.

decisions.choice: acted corruptly: ruined themselves, done what is destructive
decisions.reason: The verb means to spoil or ruin. It is used of the earth corrupted before the flood (Genesis 6:11-12) and of this same event in Deuteronomy 9:12.

decisions.choice: Go down at once / Hurry back down
decisions.reason: The two verbs "go, go down" press for haste; Balanced and Readable show it with "at once" and "hurry". Readable says "done something terrible" for "acted corruptly".

records.heading: Moses pleads for the people

records.source: סָ֣רוּ מַהֵ֗ר מִן־הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֔ם עָשׂ֣וּ לָהֶ֔ם עֵ֖גֶל מַסֵּכָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁתַּֽחֲווּ־לוֹ֙ וַיִּזְבְּחוּ־ל֔וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵ֤לֶּה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶֽעֱל֖וּךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: They have turned aside quickly from the way which I commanded them. They have made for themselves a calf of cast metal and have bowed down to it and have sacrificed to it and have said, these [are] your gods, Israel, who brought you up from [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: So soon they have left the path I laid down for them! They have cast a metal calf for themselves, bowed down before it, offered sacrifices to it, and declared, 'Israel, these are your gods, who brought you up from the land of Egypt!'"

L.8: They have turned aside quickly from the way that I commanded them. They have made for themselves a calf of cast metal and have bowed down to it and sacrificed to it and said, 'These [are] your gods, O Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.'"

R.8: They have been quick to stop doing what I commanded them. They have made themselves a calf out of melted metal. They have bowed down to it and offered sacrifices to it. They say, 'Israel, here are your gods who brought you out of Egypt!'"

decisions.choice: turned aside quickly from the way I commanded: the covenant broken within weeks
decisions.reason: God had just commanded, "You shall have no other gods before me" and "You shall not make for yourself a carved image" (20:3-4), and "gods of gold you shall not make" (20:23). The people promised to keep his words (24:3, 7), and before Moses came down they had broken them.

decisions.choice: turned aside from the way: stopped living as God commanded
decisions.reason: The way is the path of life God laid out in his commands (Deuteronomy 9:12, 16; 31:29).

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה רָאִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה עַם־קְשֵׁה־עֹ֖רֶף הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, I have seen the people this, and look, a people stiff of neck [is] it.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} went on to say to Moses, "I have seen what this people is like. They are a stiff-necked people.

L.9: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "I have seen this people, and look, a stiff-necked people it [is].

R.9: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "I have been watching these people. They are stubborn and refuse to obey.

decisions.choice: stiff-necked: stubborn, refusing to be led
decisions.reason: The picture is of an ox or donkey that stiffens its neck against the yoke or the driver's lead. Israel is called this again in 33:3, 5 and 34:9, and in Deuteronomy 9:6, 13.

decisions.choice: stubborn and refuse to obey
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m1). Literal and Balanced keep "stiff-necked", which is still understood in English.

records.source: וְעַתָּה֙ הַנִּ֣יחָה לִּ֔י וְיִֽחַר־אַפִּ֥י בָהֶ֖ם וַאֲכַלֵּ֑ם וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה אוֹתְךָ֖ לְג֥וֹי גָּדֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: And now leave me alone, that may burn my anger against them and I may consume them, and I will make you into a nation great.
pieces: So now let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} alone, so that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath can burn hot against them and I can put an end to them. Then I will make you into a great nation."

L.10: And now, let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} alone, that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger may burn hot against them and I may consume them; and I will make you into a great nation."

R.10: Now do not try to stop {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I am so angry with them that I will destroy them. Then I will make your family into a great nation."

decisions.choice: let me alone: God leaves room for Moses to plead
decisions.reason: God tells Moses to leave him alone, as if Moses could hold him back. The words announce judgment, yet they also invite the plea that follows (verses 11-13). Later Scripture remembers that Moses "stood in the breach" before God to turn away his wrath (Psalm 106:23; Deuteronomy 9:19-20, 25-26).

decisions.choice: I will make you into a great nation: the promise to Abraham, offered to Moses
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham, "I will make you into a great nation" (Genesis 12:2). Here God offers to begin again with Moses alone. Moses refuses, appealing to the promise to Abraham, Isaac and Israel (verse 13).

decisions.choice: do not try to stop me ... your family
decisions.reason: Readable says what "let me alone" means here, and "your family" for "you", since a nation would come from Moses' descendants.

records.source: וַיְחַ֣ל מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶת־פְּנֵ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לָמָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ יֶחֱרֶ֤ה אַפְּךָ֙ בְּעַמֶּ֔ךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הוֹצֵ֨אתָ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּכֹ֥חַ גָּד֖וֹל וּבְיָ֥ד חֲזָקָֽה׃
records.gloss: And implored Moses [the] face of Yahweh his God and said, why, Yahweh, does burn your anger against your people whom you brought out from [the] land of Egypt with power great and with a hand strong?
pieces: But Moses sought the favor of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God. "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}," he said, "why should {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger blaze against {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own people? You brought them out of the land of Egypt by great power and a strong hand.

L.11: And Moses implored the face of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God and said, "Why, O {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, does {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger burn against {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought out from the land of Egypt with great power and with a strong hand?

R.11: But Moses begged {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God to be kind. He said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} so angry with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people? You used {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power and strength to bring them out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: implored the face of Yahweh: sought his favor
decisions.reason: The phrase means to soften someone's face, that is, to seek the favor of someone who is angry (1 Samuel 13:12; 1 Kings 13:6). It is a different verb from the "entreat" of the plague stories (8:4).

decisions.choice: your people, whom you brought out: Moses hands God's words back to him
decisions.reason: God had called them Moses' people, whom Moses brought up (verse 7). Moses answers that they are God's people, and that God brought them out by his own great power and strong hand (6:1; 13:9).

decisions.choice: implored (Literal); sought the favor of (Balanced); begged ... to be kind (Readable)
decisions.reason: This verb is not the one rendered "entreat", "plead with" and "pray to" in the plague stories, so the levels use other words that bring out the asking for favor (m1).

records.source: לָמָּה֩ יֹאמְר֨וּ מִצְרַ֜יִם לֵאמֹ֗ר בְּרָעָ֤ה הֽוֹצִיאָם֙ לַהֲרֹ֤ג אֹתָם֙ בֶּֽהָרִ֔ים וּ֨לְכַלֹּתָ֔ם מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֑ה שׁ֚וּב מֵחֲר֣וֹן אַפֶּ֔ךָ וְהִנָּחֵ֥ם עַל־הָרָעָ֖ה לְעַמֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Why should say Egypt, saying, with evil he brought them out, to kill them in the mountains and to consume them from upon [the] face of the ground? Turn from [the] burning of your anger and relent concerning the harm to your people.
pieces: Why should the Egyptians say, 'He brought them out to do them harm, to kill them among the mountains and put an end to them on the face of the earth'? Turn from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fierce anger, and relent from the harm {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} mean to bring on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people.

L.12: Why should Egypt say, 'With evil [intent] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them out, to kill them in the mountains and to consume them from upon the face of the ground'? Turn from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} burning anger, and relent concerning the harm to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people.

R.12: Do not let the Egyptians say, 'He led them out only to hurt them. He wanted to kill them in the mountains and destroy every one of them.' Please stop being so angry! Change {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mind, and do not bring this harm on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people.

decisions.choice: with evil ... the harm: one word, used twice
decisions.reason: The same word means "evil" and "harm" or "disaster". Moses asks God not to do the "harm" that would let the Egyptians say he brought Israel out with "evil" intent: God's name among the nations is at stake (compare 9:16; Numbers 14:13-16).

decisions.choice: relent: change course, turn from what was intended
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in verse 14, where the note explains it.

decisions.choice: the Egyptians
decisions.reason: "Egypt" here means the people of Egypt; Balanced and Readable say "the Egyptians". Readable says "Change your mind" for "relent", as in verse 14.

records.source: זְכֹ֡ר לְאַבְרָהָם֩ לְיִצְחָ֨ק וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל עֲבָדֶ֗יךָ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֣עְתָּ לָהֶם֮ בָּךְ֒ וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אַרְבֶּה֙ אֶֽת־זַרְעֲכֶ֔ם כְּכוֹכְבֵ֖י הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְכָל־הָאָ֨רֶץ הַזֹּ֜את אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֗רְתִּי אֶתֵּן֙ לְזַרְעֲכֶ֔ם וְנָחֲל֖וּ לְעֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: Remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself and said to them, I will multiply your offspring like [the] stars of the heavens, and all the land this which I have said I will give to your offspring, and they will possess [it] forever.
pieces: Remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel, who served {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You swore to them by {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} and told them, 'I will make your descendants as many as the stars in the sky. All this land I have spoken of I will give to your descendants, and it will be theirs for all time.'"

L.13: Remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants, to whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} swore by {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} and said to them, 'I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens, and all this land that I have spoken of I will give to your offspring, and they shall possess [it] forever.'"

R.13: Remember {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. You made them a promise and swore by {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}. You said, 'I will give you more descendants than there are stars in the sky. I will give your descendants all this land I promised, and it will belong to them forever.'"

decisions.choice: you swore by yourself ... like the stars: God's oath to the fathers
decisions.reason: After Abraham offered Isaac, God swore by himself to multiply his offspring like the stars of the heavens (Genesis 22:16-17; see also 15:5; 26:4). The land was promised to Abraham and his offspring (Genesis 12:7; 13:15; 28:13). With no one greater to swear by, God swore by himself (Hebrews 6:13).

decisions.choice: Israel: Jacob
decisions.reason: Israel is the name God gave Jacob (Genesis 35:10), and the people are named after him.

decisions.choice: Jacob
decisions.reason: Readable uses the patriarch's more familiar name, so readers do not confuse him with the people (m2).

records.source: וַיִּנָּ֖חֶם יְהוָ֑ה עַל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֖ר לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לְעַמּֽוֹ׃פ
records.gloss: And relented Yahweh concerning the harm which he had spoken to do to his people.
pieces: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} relented from the harm {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would do to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

L.14: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} relented concerning the harm that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken of doing to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

R.14: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} changed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind. He did not do the harm {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would do to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

decisions.choice: relented: God's response, told in human terms
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in Genesis 6:6 for God's regret. It means to change course or to turn from what was intended. The Bible says God does not change his mind as a human does (Numbers 23:19; 1 Samuel 15:29), yet it often says he relents when people turn or when someone pleads for them (Jeremiah 18:7-10; Jonah 3:10; Amos 7:3, 6). This does not mean God was mistaken or did not foresee events. It shows that he truly answers prayer: Moses pleaded, and the judgment threatened in verse 10 was not carried out.

decisions.choice: the harm he had spoken of: the destruction threatened in verse 10
decisions.reason: The word means harm or disaster here, not moral evil.

decisions.choice: changed his mind
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday phrase; Literal and Balanced say "relented". "Repented" is avoided at every level, since in English it suggests turning from sin.

records.source: וַיִּ֜פֶן וַיֵּ֤רֶד מֹשֶׁה֙ מִן־הָהָ֔ר וּשְׁנֵ֛י לֻחֹ֥ת הָעֵדֻ֖ת בְּיָד֑וֹ לֻחֹ֗ת כְּתֻבִים֙ מִשְּׁנֵ֣י עֶבְרֵיהֶ֔ם מִזֶּ֥ה וּמִזֶּ֖ה הֵ֥ם כְּתֻבִֽים׃
records.gloss: And turned and went down Moses from the mountain, and [the] two tablets of the testimony [were] in his hand, tablets written on both their sides; on this and on this they [were] written.
pieces: Then Moses turned and went down from the mountain, holding the two tablets of the testimony. These tablets were written on both sides, on the one face and on the other.

L.15: And Moses turned and went down from the mountain, and the two tablets of the testimony [were] in his hand, tablets written on both their sides; on this [side] and on that [side] they were written.

R.15: Moses turned and went down the mountain. In his hands he carried the two stone tablets of the covenant. There was writing on both sides of them, front and back.

decisions.choice: the tablets of the testimony: the stone tablets bearing the covenant
decisions.reason: These are the tablets God gave Moses in 31:18, written with the covenant words, God's witness to the covenant (25:16).

decisions.choice: written on both sides: the whole text, front and back
decisions.reason: Writing on both faces of a tablet was unusual. It may stress that the tablets were full and complete, with nothing to be added.

decisions.choice: the two stone tablets of the covenant
decisions.reason: As in 31:18, Readable says "of the covenant" for "of the testimony". It says "hands", since Moses carried two tablets.

records.heading: Moses breaks the tablets

records.source: וְהַ֨לֻּחֹ֔ת מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים הֵ֑מָּה וְהַמִּכְתָּ֗ב מִכְתַּ֤ב אֱלֹהִים֙ ה֔וּא חָר֖וּת עַל־הַלֻּחֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And the tablets [were the] work of God they, and the writing [was the] writing of God it, engraved on the tablets.
pieces: God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} had made the tablets, and the writing cut into them was God's own writing.

L.16: And the tablets, they [were] the work of God, and the writing, it [was] the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.

R.16: God had made the tablets. God had cut the words into them in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own writing.

decisions.choice: the work of God ... the writing of God: made and written by God himself
decisions.reason: The double phrase stresses that neither the tablets nor the words came from Moses. They were written "by the finger of God" (31:18). That makes their breaking in verse 19 all the more striking.

decisions.choice: engraved: cut into the stone
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here in the Old Testament. It is related to words for carving, and means cut or incised.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֧ע יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ אֶת־ק֥וֹל הָעָ֖ם בְּרֵעֹ֑הוַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה ק֥וֹל מִלְחָמָ֖ה בַּֽמַּחֲנֶה׃
records.gloss: And heard Joshua the sound of the people in its shouting, and he said to Moses, a sound of war [is] in the camp.
pieces: When Joshua heard the noise of the people shouting, he said to Moses, "I hear the sound of war in the camp!"

L.17: And Joshua heard the sound of the people in their shouting, and he said to Moses, "A sound of war [is] in the camp!"

R.17: Joshua heard the people shouting. He said to Moses, "It sounds as if there is fighting in the camp!"

decisions.choice: Joshua: Moses' assistant, who had gone part of the way up with him
decisions.reason: Joshua went up the mountain with Moses (24:13) and seems to have waited below the cloud. He knew nothing of what God had told Moses, so he thinks first of an attack, as at Rephidim (17:8-13).

decisions.choice: shouting: a loud noise of many voices
decisions.reason: The word can describe a battle cry or a crowd's uproar. Joshua takes it for the first.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֵ֥ין קוֹל֙ עֲנ֣וֹת גְּבוּרָ֔ה וְאֵ֥ין ק֖וֹל עֲנ֣וֹת חֲלוּשָׁ֑ה ק֣וֹל עַנּ֔וֹת אָנֹכִ֖י שֹׁמֵֽעַ׃
records.gloss: And he said, not [is it the] sound of answering of strength, and not [the] sound of answering of weakness; [the] sound of singing I [am] hearing.
pieces: But Moses answered, "It is not the shout of men who have won, nor the wail of men who have lost. What I hear is the sound of singing."

L.18: And he said, "[It is] not the sound of a shout of victory, and [it is] not the sound of a cry of defeat; the sound of singing I am hearing."

R.18: Moses answered, "That is not the noise of soldiers cheering because they won. It is not the noise of soldiers crying because they lost. It is the noise of people singing."

decisions.choice: victory ... defeat ... singing: a play on one word, whose last sense is uncertain
alternatives: the sound of revelry I hear
the sound of people singing in turn I hear
decisions.reason: Moses answers in three short lines built on one verb, which can mean to answer, to call out or to sing. The first two lines speak of the cry of "strength" (victory) and of "weakness" (defeat). The third uses a different form of the same verb, and its exact sense is not certain: singing, perhaps answering back and forth as a choir does, or a word meaning wild or mocking shouts. Moses knows from God what is happening (verses 7-8) and corrects Joshua: this is not war but revelry.

decisions.choice: men who have won / soldiers cheering because they won
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose shouts the "strength" and "weakness" are: victors and losers in battle. Balanced names Moses as the speaker, since the subject changes.

records.source: וַֽיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר קָרַב֙ אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַיַּ֥רְא אֶת־הָעֵ֖גֶל וּמְחֹלֹ֑ת וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֣ף מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיַּשְׁלֵ֤ךְ מִיָּדָיו֙ אֶת־הַלֻּחֹ֔ת וַיְשַׁבֵּ֥ר אֹתָ֖ם תַּ֥חַת הָהָֽר׃
records.gloss: And it was when he drew near to the camp, and he saw the calf and dances, and burned [the] anger of Moses, and he threw from his hands the tablets and broke them beneath the mountain.
pieces: As Moses came close to the camp, he saw the calf and the people dancing. He blazed with anger, flung down the tablets he was holding, and smashed them at the foot of the mountain.

L.19: And it was, when he drew near to the camp, he saw the calf and [the] dances, and the anger of Moses burned, and he threw the tablets from his hands and broke them beneath the mountain.

R.19: As Moses came near the camp, he saw the calf and the people dancing. He became furious. He threw the tablets down and broke them into pieces at the bottom of the mountain.

decisions.choice: he broke the tablets: the covenant had been broken
decisions.reason: The tablets bore the words of the covenant (34:28). By breaking them in front of the people, Moses shows that they have broken the covenant they had sworn to keep (24:3, 7; Deuteronomy 9:16-17). God later writes the words again on new tablets (34:1).

decisions.choice: from his hands: the read form; the written form may be "his hand"
decisions.reason: The traditional Hebrew text marks a difference between the consonants as written and the form to be read here. The read form is "his hands". The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the people dancing
decisions.reason: The word means dances or dancing in groups, as with Miriam (15:20). Balanced and Readable say who was dancing.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־הָעֵ֨גֶל אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ וַיִּשְׂרֹ֣ף בָּאֵ֔שׁ וַיִּטְחַ֖ן עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁר־דָּ֑ק וַיִּ֨זֶר֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַמַּ֔יִם וַיַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And he took the calf which they had made and burned [it] with fire and ground [it] until it was fine, and scattered [it] on [the] surface of the water and made drink [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: He took the calf they had made, burned it in the fire, and crushed it until it was fine dust. Then he scattered the dust over the water and made the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} drink it.

L.20: And he took the calf that they had made and burned [it] with fire and ground [it] until [it] was fine, and scattered [it] on the surface of the water and made the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel drink [it].

R.20: Moses took the calf the people had made and burned it. He crushed what was left into dust and sprinkled it on the water. Then he made the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} drink it.

decisions.choice: burned, ground, scattered: the idol utterly destroyed
alternatives: the calf was melted and broken up, not burned to ash
decisions.reason: The calf was perhaps a wooden figure covered in gold, which would burn, or the fire was used to melt and break up the metal. Deuteronomy 9:21 tells how Moses ground it to dust and threw the dust into the stream that came down from the mountain. Nothing was left that could be worshiped again (compare 2 Kings 23:6, 15).

decisions.choice: made them drink it: the people swallow their own sin
decisions.reason: The people are made to take the remains of their idol into their own bodies. The act shames the idol and the people together. It may also recall the ordeal of bitter water in Numbers 5:16-28, by which hidden guilt was revealed.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֔ן מֶֽה־עָשָׂ֥ה לְךָ֖ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּֽי־הֵבֵ֥אתָ עָלָ֖יו חֲטָאָ֥ה גְדֹלָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Moses to Aaron, what did to you the people this, that you have brought on it a sin great?
pieces: Moses asked Aaron, "What had this people done to you, that you would bring so great a sin on them?"

L.21: And Moses said to Aaron, "What did this people do to you, that you have brought on it a great sin?"

R.21: Moses asked Aaron, "What did these people do to you? Why did you lead them into such a terrible sin?"

decisions.choice: a great sin: a grave offense against God
decisions.reason: "A great sin" is used of serious wrongs, such as adultery (Genesis 20:9) and idolatry (2 Kings 17:21). Moses uses the phrase again in verses 30-31.

decisions.choice: you have brought on it: Aaron is held responsible
decisions.reason: The question puts the blame on Aaron as leader: by doing what the people asked, he led them into sin, as if he wished them harm.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַהֲרֹ֔ן אַל־יִ֥חַר אַ֖ף אֲדֹנִ֑י אַתָּה֙ יָדַ֣עְתָּ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם כִּ֥י בְרָ֖ע הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And said Aaron, not let burn [the] anger of my lord; you know the people, that on evil it [is].
pieces: Aaron answered, "My lord, do not be so angry. You yourself know this people, how bent they are on doing wrong.

L.22: And Aaron said, "Let not the anger of my lord burn. You know the people, that it [is set] on evil.

R.22: Aaron answered, "Sir, please do not be angry. You know how these people are always ready to do evil.

decisions.choice: on evil it is: set on doing wrong
decisions.reason: The phrase means the people are inclined to evil. Aaron shifts the blame from himself to the people.

decisions.choice: my lord: a respectful address to Moses
decisions.reason: Aaron, the elder brother, addresses Moses as a servant addresses a master. The title here is used of a human and is not the divine name.

decisions.choice: Sir
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday word of respect for "my lord", which could be taken as a name for God.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ לִ֔י עֲשֵׂה־לָ֣נוּ אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֵלְכ֖וּ לְפָנֵ֑ינוּ כִּי־זֶ֣ה׀מֹשֶׁ֣ה הָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶֽעֱלָ֨נוּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְנוּ מֶה־הָ֥יָה לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And they said to me, make for us gods who will go before us, for this Moses, the man who brought us up from [the] land of Egypt, not we know what has happened to him.
pieces: They said to me, 'Make us gods to lead the way for us. This Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt, we have no idea what has become of him.'

L.23: And they said to me, 'Make for us gods who will go before us, for this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.'

R.23: They said to me, 'Make us gods to lead us. We do not know what has happened to Moses, the man who led us out of Egypt.'

decisions.choice: Aaron repeats the people's words
decisions.reason: Aaron repeats the request of verse 1 almost word for word, but leaves out his own part in the gathering of the gold and the making of the calf (verse 4). On the plural "gods", see verse 1.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֤ר לָהֶם֙ לְמִ֣י זָהָ֔ב הִתְפָּרָ֖קוּ וַיִּתְּנוּ־לִ֑י וָאַשְׁלִכֵ֣הוּ בָאֵ֔שׁ וַיֵּצֵ֖א הָעֵ֥גֶל הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And I said to them, to whom [is] gold? Tear [it] off from yourselves. And they gave [it] to me, and I threw it into the fire, and came out the calf this.
pieces: So I told them, 'Anyone who has gold, pull it off.' They handed it over to me, I tossed it into the fire, and out came this calf!"

L.24: And I said to them, 'Whoever [has] gold, tear [it] off.' And they gave [it] to me, and I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf."

R.24: So I told them, 'If you have any gold, take it off.' They gave me their gold. I threw it into the fire, and this calf came out!"

decisions.choice: out came this calf: Aaron's excuse against the narrator's account
decisions.reason: Verse 4 says Aaron took the gold, worked it with a tool and made it into a calf. In his own telling the calf came out of the fire by itself. The gap between the two shows Aaron trying to excuse himself.

records.source: וַיַּ֤רְא מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם כִּ֥י פָרֻ֖עַ ה֑וּא כִּֽי־פְרָעֹ֣ה אַהֲרֹ֔ן לְשִׁמְצָ֖ה בְּקָמֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And saw Moses the people, that broken loose it [was], for had let it loose Aaron, for derision among those who rise against them.
pieces: Moses saw that the people had broken loose. Aaron had let them run unchecked, so that they had become something for their enemies to sneer at.

L.25: And Moses saw the people, that it [was] broken loose, for Aaron had let it loose, for a derision among those who rise against them.

R.25: Moses saw that the people were out of control. Aaron had let them do whatever they wanted. Now their enemies would laugh at them.

decisions.choice: broken loose: without restraint, out of control
decisions.reason: The verb means to let loose, as hair is let down (Leviticus 10:6), or to throw off restraint (Proverbs 29:18). The people have thrown off the bounds God set, and Aaron, their leader in Moses' absence, let it happen.

decisions.choice: a derision among those who rise against them: a disgrace before their enemies
alternatives: to the joy of their enemies
decisions.reason: The word translated "derision" occurs only here, and its exact sense is uncertain: a whisper of scorn or a cause of mockery. "Those who rise against them" are their enemies.

records.source: וַיַּעֲמֹ֤ד מֹשֶׁה֙ בְּשַׁ֣עַר הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֥י לַיהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י וַיֵּאָסְפ֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו כָּל־בְּנֵ֥י לֵוִֽי׃
records.gloss: And stood Moses in [the] gate of the camp and said, who [is] for Yahweh? To me! And gathered to him all [the] sons of Levi.
pieces: Moses took his stand at the gate of the camp and called out, "Who is on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s side? Come here to me!" And all the Levites rallied around him.

L.26: And Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, "Who [is] for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? To me!" And all the sons of Levi gathered to him.

R.26: So Moses stood at the entrance of the camp and shouted, "Whoever is loyal to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, come over to me!" All the men from the tribe of Levi gathered around him.

decisions.choice: who is for Yahweh: who will take Yahweh's side
decisions.reason: Moses calls those who belong to Yahweh to stand with him against the idolatry. The call divides the camp.

decisions.choice: the sons of Levi: Moses' own tribe
decisions.reason: Moses and Aaron were of the tribe of Levi (2:1; 6:16-20). Jacob had cursed Levi's violence (Genesis 34:25-30; 49:5-7). Here that zeal is turned to God's service, and Levi is later set apart for it (Numbers 3:5-13; Deuteronomy 33:8-11).

decisions.choice: the Levites / the men from the tribe of Levi
decisions.reason: The "sons of Levi" are the members of the tribe, here the men who took up swords (verse 27). Literal keeps "sons of Levi".

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שִׂ֥ימוּ אִישׁ־חַרְבּ֖וֹ עַל־יְרֵכ֑וֹ עִבְר֨וּ וָשׁ֜וּבוּ מִשַּׁ֤עַר לָשַׁ֨עַר֙ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וְהִרְג֧וּ אִֽישׁ־אֶת־אָחִ֛יו וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶת־רֵעֵ֖הוּ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶת־קְרֹבֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he said to them, thus says Yahweh, [the] God of Israel, put each man his sword on his thigh, pass through and return from gate to gate in the camp, and kill each man his brother and each man his friend and each man his neighbor.
pieces: He said to them, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: 'Every man of you fasten his sword at his side. Pass through the camp from gate to gate and back again. Kill, every one of you, your brother, your friend and your neighbor.'"

L.27: And he said to them, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: 'Put each man his sword on his thigh; pass through and return from gate to gate in the camp, and kill each man his brother and each man his friend and each man his neighbor.'"

R.27: He told them, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says, 'Each of you must strap on his sword. Go through the whole camp, from one gate to the other and back. Kill your brothers, your friends and your neighbors.'"

decisions.choice: kill each man his brother, friend and neighbor: judgment carried out by the people's own kin
decisions.reason: The command is meant plainly: the Levites were to kill those in the camp who had given themselves to the idol, sparing no one for family ties. The covenant law had just said that anyone who sacrificed to other gods was to be destroyed (22:19), and Deuteronomy 13:6-11 later commands that not even a brother or a friend be spared who leads others to other gods. Deuteronomy 33:9 praises Levi for not recognizing brother or son in this. The text does not say how those who were killed were chosen; verse 25 and verse 35 suggest those who had broken loose in the worship of the calf.

decisions.choice: put his sword on his thigh: arm himself
decisions.reason: The sword was worn in a belt hanging at the hip (Judges 3:16; 2 Samuel 20:8).

decisions.choice: at his side / strap on his sword
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where a sword was worn, at the side; Literal keeps "thigh". No level softens the command to kill.

records.source: וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֥וּ בְנֵֽי־לֵוִ֖י כִּדְבַ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּפֹּ֤ל מִן־הָעָם֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא כִּשְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אַלְפֵ֖י אִֽישׁ׃
records.gloss: And did [the] sons of Levi according to [the] word of Moses, and fell of the people on day that about three thousands of men.
pieces: The Levites did as Moses ordered, and about 3,000 men of the people were killed that day.

L.28: And the sons of Levi did according to the word of Moses, and there fell of the people on that day about 3,000 men.

R.28: The men of Levi obeyed Moses. That day they killed about 3,000 men.

decisions.choice: fell ... about three thousand men: about three thousand were killed
decisions.reason: "Fell" means fell dead, struck down by the sword. The number is given as an approximate figure.

decisions.choice: were killed / they killed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what "fell" means here (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה מִלְא֨וּ יֶדְכֶ֤ם הַיּוֹם֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ בִּבְנ֖וֹ וּבְאָחִ֑יו וְלָתֵ֧ת עֲלֵיכֶ֛ם הַיּ֖וֹם בְּרָכָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Moses, fill your hand today for Yahweh, for each man [was] against his son and against his brother, and to give upon you today a blessing.
pieces: Moses said, "Today you have ordained yourselves for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for each of you took a stand against his own son and brother. And so this day a blessing has been given you."

L.29: And Moses said, "[You have] filled your hand today for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for each man [was] against his son and against his brother, so as to bring upon you today a blessing."

R.29: Moses said, "Today you have been set apart to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Each of you stood against his own son or brother. Because of this, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed you today."

decisions.choice: fill your hand: ordain, install in office
decisions.reason: To "fill the hand" is to install someone as a priest (28:41; 29:9). By their act the Levites were set apart for the service of Yahweh, and later the whole tribe is given to serve at the tabernacle (Numbers 3:5-13; 8:14-19).

decisions.choice: fill: read as a statement of what the Levites' deed has done
alternatives: Fill your hand today for Yahweh (ordain yourselves today)
decisions.reason: As the Hebrew text is pointed, the verb is a command, "Fill your hand today": ordain yourselves. But the deed is already done (verse 28), and the ancient Greek and Latin translations read a statement, "You have filled your hands today". Either way the sense is that by this day's act the Levites are installed for Yahweh's service.

decisions.choice: to give upon you a blessing: so that God has blessed you
decisions.reason: The infinitive gives the result of their act: they have received a blessing, which is God's to give.

decisions.choice: set apart to serve ... the LORD has blessed you
decisions.reason: Readable explains "filled your hand" and names the LORD as the giver of the blessing, which the Hebrew implies (m3).

records.source: וַיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם אַתֶּ֥ם חֲטָאתֶ֖ם חֲטָאָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֑ה וְעַתָּה֙ אֶֽעֱלֶ֣ה אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה אוּלַ֥י אֲכַפְּרָ֖ה בְּעַ֥ד חַטַּאתְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And it was on [the] next day, and said Moses to the people, you have sinned a sin great, and now I will go up to Yahweh; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin.
pieces: The next day Moses told the people, "What you have done is a terrible sin. But I will go up again to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It may be that I can make atonement for your sin."

L.30: And it was on the next day, and Moses said to the people, "You, you have sinned a great sin. And now I will go up to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin."

R.30: The next day Moses said to the people, "You have done something very wicked. But I will go back up to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Perhaps I can make atonement for your sin, so that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will forgive you."

decisions.choice: make atonement: cover the sin, set things right with God
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the priests' atoning sacrifices (29:36; 30:10). Here Moses means to do it by pleading with God, offering even himself (verse 32). "Perhaps" shows he cannot be sure God will accept it.

decisions.choice: so that the LORD will forgive you
decisions.reason: Readable adds the purpose of atonement, forgiveness, which Moses asks for in verse 32.

records.source: וַיָּ֧שָׁב מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אָ֣נָּ֗א חָטָ֞א הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ חֲטָאָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֔ה וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י זָהָֽב׃
records.gloss: And returned Moses to Yahweh and said, alas, has sinned the people this a sin great, and they have made for themselves gods of gold.
pieces: So Moses went back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "Oh, hear me! This people has committed a terrible sin. They have made themselves gods out of gold.

L.31: And Moses returned to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "Alas, this people has sinned a great sin, and they have made for themselves gods of gold.

R.31: So Moses went back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He said, "Please listen! These people have done something very wicked. They have made gods for themselves out of gold.

decisions.choice: alas: an urgent cry of pleading
decisions.reason: The word opens a desperate request, "O please!" (Genesis 50:17; Nehemiah 1:5, 11).

decisions.choice: gods of gold: what the covenant forbade
decisions.reason: Moses confesses the sin in the very words of the law: "Gods of gold you shall not make for yourselves" (20:23). On the plural, see verse 1.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֖ה אִם־תִּשָּׂ֣א חַטָּאתָ֑ם וְאִם־אַ֕יִן מְחֵ֣נִי נָ֔א מִֽסִּפְרְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּתָֽבְתָּ׃
records.gloss: And now if you will forgive their sin—; and if not, blot me out please from your book which you have written.
pieces: But now, if only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would forgive their sin! But if not, then blot me out of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} book that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have written."

L.32: And now, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will forgive their sin— and if not, blot me out, please, from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} book that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have written."

R.32: Please forgive their sin. But if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not, then erase my name from the book {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have written."

decisions.choice: if you will forgive their sin—: a sentence left unfinished
alternatives: if you will forgive their sin, forgive it
decisions.reason: Moses does not finish the first "if". The broken sentence is itself a plea: if you will forgive them, then do so. The second "if" offers his own life instead.

decisions.choice: blot me out of your book: take my life with theirs
decisions.reason: God's book is the list of the living, those who belong to him (Isaiah 4:3; Daniel 12:1; Philippians 4:3; Revelation 3:5). Moses asks to die with his people rather than be spared without them; compare Paul's wish in Romans 9:3.

decisions.choice: Please forgive ... erase my name
decisions.reason: Readable turns the unfinished sentence into the plea it implies (m1), and says "erase my name" for "blot me out".

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה מִ֚י אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָֽטָא־לִ֔י אֶמְחֶ֖נּוּ מִסִּפְרִֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, whoever has sinned against me, I will blot him out from my book.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered Moses, "It is the one who has sinned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} whom I will blot out of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} book.

L.33: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Whoever has sinned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, him I will blot out of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} book.

R.33: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered Moses, "I will erase from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} book only the names of those who have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: whoever has sinned against me: each answers for his own sin
decisions.reason: God refuses Moses' offer to take the people's place. The one who sinned is the one who will be blotted out (compare Deuteronomy 24:16; Ezekiel 18:4, 20).

decisions.choice: only the names of those
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain the contrast with Moses' offer: those who sinned, not Moses.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֞ה לֵ֣ךְ׀נְחֵ֣ה אֶת־הָעָ֗ם אֶ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ לָ֔ךְ הִנֵּ֥ה מַלְאָכִ֖י יֵלֵ֣ךְ לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וּבְי֣וֹם פָּקְדִ֔י וּפָקַדְתִּ֥י עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם חַטָּאתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And now go, lead the people to [the place] which I have spoken to you. Look, my angel will go before you. And on [the] day of my visiting, I will visit on them their sin.
pieces: Now go and lead the people to the place I told you of. My angel will go ahead of you. But when the day comes for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to call them to account, I will call them to account for their sin."

L.34: And now go, lead the people to [the place] of which I have spoken to you. Look, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} angel will go before you. And in the day of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} visiting, I will visit their sin upon them."

R.34: Now go and lead the people to the land I promised. My angel will go in front of you. But a day is coming when I will punish them for their sin."

decisions.choice: my angel will go before you: the guide promised in 23:20
decisions.reason: God had promised to send his angel before Israel to bring them into the land (23:20, 23). The promise stands, but in 33:2-3 God says he will not go up among them himself, because of their sin, and Moses pleads that he will (33:12-16).

decisions.choice: visit: attend to, here to punish
decisions.reason: The verb means to give attention to someone, for good (3:16; 4:31) or for punishment, as in 20:5. The sin is pardoned for now, but not ignored; God will call it to account at a time of his choosing.

decisions.choice: call them to account / punish
decisions.reason: "Visit" no longer carries this sense in English. Balanced says "call to account", and Readable "punish". Literal keeps "visit". Readable says "the land I promised" for "the place I have spoken of".

records.source: וַיִּגֹּ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־הָעָ֑ם עַ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשׂ֣וּ אֶת־הָעֵ֔גֶל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה אַהֲרֹֽן׃ס
records.gloss: And struck Yahweh the people because they had made the calf which had made Aaron.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent a plague on the people for making the calf, the calf that Aaron had made.

L.35: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck the people, because they had made the calf that Aaron made.

R.35: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} punished the people with a plague, because they had made the calf. Aaron was the one who made it.

decisions.choice: struck: a blow from God, often a plague
alternatives: struck the people (the form of the blow not named)
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike or smite, and is used of the plagues on Egypt (12:23, 27). The text does not say what form this blow took, or whether it is the punishment announced in verse 34 or a first part of it.

decisions.choice: they had made the calf that Aaron made: both are guilty
decisions.reason: The people made the calf by asking for it and giving their gold; Aaron made it with his own hands. The verse holds both responsible.

decisions.choice: sent a plague / punished with a plague
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "plague" for the blow, as the verb often means. Literal keeps "struck".
